comments.content: The prompt text is being JSON.stringify'd before being submitted, which will wrap the text in quotes and escape internal characters (e.g., newlines become \n, quotes become \"). Since `result.messages[0].content.text` is already a string, this will send a malformed prompt to the model. Use the raw text directly: `content: result.messages[0].content.text`.

This only handles `result.messages[0].content.text`, but MCP prompt responses can contain multiple messages and non-text content types (e.g., image, resource). Consider concatenating text across all messages, or at least documenting that only the first text message is used. As written, multi-message prompts silently lose data.

Arguments are parsed only via `--key=value` syntax. MCP prompt arguments are commonly positional. Also, `if (value)` treats an empty-string value (e.g. `--key=""`) as missing, which will incorrectly trigger the required-argument error for intentionally empty values. Consider checking `value !== undefined` instead of truthiness.

Removing the `if (discoveredTools.length === 0) throw Error('No enabled tools found')` check changes discovery behavior: servers that expose only prompts (and no tools) will no longer throw. Verify that downstream callers of discoverTools/connectAndDiscover correctly handle the now-possible empty tools array, since prior code relied on this throw to mark servers appropriately.
